result.title: Self-Replicating Language Models
result.comment: About 64 pages, 16 figures, 2 tables. Under review at Artificial Life
result.summary: Whether large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are a form of life is a scientifically interesting question. Under the Darwinian definition of life, it is also a practical one, because a system capable of Darwinian Evolution can adapt. We therefore test several modes in which a language model can reproduce itself: by emitting a genome that trains its offspring, by copying and mutating its own weights, and by teaching a child from its own samples. In principle, small language models can replicate and evolve: selection improves them, and they adapt to narrow niches. Selection also lowers mutation rates, and a language model, unlike any organism, can lower its own to zero, which may limit its evolution. Flagship LLMs can write such replicators, but for a large LLM to replicate by teaching its offspring remains, for now, technically and economically infeasible.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察语言模型自我复制的几种模式——输出可训练子代的基因组、复制并突变自身权重、用自身样本教学——并检验其达尔文式选择、适应与突变率变化。
